close_reason: Implemented option A from the bead: tightened ChatBackend::expire_message return type from Result<(), BackendSetError<Self::Error>> to Result<(), Self::Error>. The NotFound SetError variant is no longer constructible on this path, so the idempotency contract is type-enforced (rustdoc upgraded from SHOULD to MUST). Bonus: while refactoring the burn-on-read call site in handle_message_set, routed the burn_err description through server_fail_value_from_backend per workspace redaction discipline — this closes the redaction-discipline leak at message.rs:853-864 that JMAP-x2gd.91 (P1) flagged. No analog in mail-server (expire_message is chat-spec only). 22 backend.rs unit tests + 170 integration tests + workspace tests all pass. Commit 23a9a32.
description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:752-762, 781-788

  /// # Idempotency
  ///
  /// If the message no longer exists — because a previous
  /// expire_message call or an atomic update_object
  /// implementation has already deleted it — this method SHOULD
  /// return Ok(()) rather than
  /// BackendSetError::SetError(SetError::NotFound). Expiry events
  /// are inherently retry-friendly...
  fn expire_message(
      &self,
      _caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
      _account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
      _message_id: &jmap_types::Id,
  ) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = Result<(), BackendSetError<Self::Error>>> + Send;

The contract is enforced ONLY by prose. The type system permits
the contract-violating return: BackendSetError::SetError
constructed with SetErrorType::NotFound is a perfectly typeable
value, and a naive backend implementor seeing 'message not in my
store' will return that.

The downstream consequence is already filed as a bug in this
same epic: JMAP-x2gd.6 ('Message/set burn-on-read failure
commits readAt write then reports serverFail, violating spec
MUST hard-delete'). The bug is rooted in this contract gap: the
burn-on-read handler does not differentiate
'message-already-gone (success)' from
'message-doesn't-exist (treat as serverFail)' because the type
doesn't either.

Fix options:

A. Tighten the return type:
     fn expire_message(...) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), Self::Error>> + Send;

   Drop BackendSetError entirely. Backends that hit a storage-
   layer failure (mutex poisoned, connection refused) return
   Self::Error. There is no /set-shaped error path — expire isn't
   a /set call, it's an internal scheduler hook.

B. Add an explicit ExpireOutcome enum:
     pub enum ExpireOutcome {
         Removed,
         AlreadyGone,
     }
     fn expire_message(...) -> impl Future<Output = Result<ExpireOutcome, Self::Error>> + Send;

   The handler can react differently to the two cases if a
   future use case demands. Backends can never accidentally
   surface NotFound on the success path.

C. Keep the signature, but tighten the rustdoc with a normative
   MUST and a test the handler can compile-time enforce. Weakest
   option — the contract is exactly the doc that already exists.

Workspace AGENTS.md API-contract section ('Contract underspecification'):
'Panic conditions that should be Result::Err, or that are
documented only in implementation comments rather than in the
public docstring' — flipped variant applies here: behaviors that
SHOULD NOT be Result::Err but the type permits.

Option A is the cleanest fix and the backend-canonical-error
posture matches the rest of the trait's optional hooks
(is_contact_blocked, slow_mode_check) that don't return
BackendSetError.
title: API contract: expire_message doc says SHOULD return Ok(()) on not-found but type permits NotFound
